definitions.explanation: An older person, typically referring to someone in their senior years. Can sometimes sound slightly informal or even mildly impolite depending on context.

examples.japanese: {年寄|としよ}りには{席|せき}を{譲|ゆず}りましょう。
examples.english: Let's give up our seats for elderly people.

examples.japanese: {祖父|そふ}は{年寄|としよ}りでも{元気|げんき}だ。
examples.english: My grandfather is still energetic despite being elderly.

examples.japanese: {年寄|としよ}り{扱|あつか}いしないでください。
examples.english: Please don't treat me like an old person.

notes:
USAGE: {年寄|としよ}り is a common word but can sound somewhat informal or even mildly disrespectful in certain contexts. More polite alternatives exist.

POLITER ALTERNATIVES:
・お{年寄|としよ}り (more polite, with お)
・{高齢者|こうれいしゃ} (senior citizen - formal/official)
・{老人|ろうじん} (old person - neutral but clinical)
・ご{年配|ねんぱい}の{方|かた} (elderly person - very polite)
・シニア (senior - loanword)

COMMON PATTERNS:
・お{年寄|としよ}り (elderly people - polite)
・{年寄|としよ}り{臭|くさ}い (old-fashioned, like an old person)
・{年寄|としよ}りの{冷|ひ}や{水|みず} (an old person acting young - idiom)

NOTE: Be careful with usage. {高齢者|こうれいしゃ} is preferred in formal or official contexts. お{年寄|としよ}り is acceptable in daily conversation.
